title: Evening non-caffeine tea ritual
hypothesis: A consistent non-caffeine evening tea ritual 60–90 minutes before bed will improve subjective wind-down over 14 days.

intervention.summary: Prepare one cup of a non-caffeine culinary tea or herbal infusion you already tolerate; sip slowly as a wind-down cue.
steps: Pick a non-caffeine option you already use safely (e.g. rooibos, mint, ginger culinary teas — personal tolerance first).
Brew one ordinary cup per label of a food-grade product.
Sit away from bright screens if possible; journal one sentence of the day.

timing.phase_note: Avoid large fluid volume if nocturia is a problem; discuss with clinician if needed.

expected_effect.note: Ritual and caffeine avoidance may matter more than the specific culinary herb.

stop_conditions: Pregnancy or medication interaction concerns raised by clinician or pharmacist
Any product that is not ordinary food-grade tea
contraindications: Clinician or pharmacist advised avoidance of specific herbs
Use of non-food 'plant medicine' preparations — out of scope; jurisdiction routing only
